name: Tidal and wave energy
principle: Turbines or oscillating devices capture tidal streams and waves. Orbital Marine's 2 MW O2 floating tidal turbine is anchored in the Fall of Warness at the European Marine Energy Centre, Orkney, and feeds the local grid by subsea cable.

process_steps.name: Device captures tidal or wave energy

performance.basis: anchored at EMEC Fall of Warness

source.note: Orbital Marine Power, O2 page, read 25 October 2026
IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, latest assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Tidal stream (ocean current energy)' 6 (2025); 'Wave energy converters (wave energy)' 6 (2025)

limitations: The O2 page gives no start-up date

reference_plants.name: La Rance tidal barrage, France
reference_plants.capacity: 240 MW (24 x 10 MW bulb turbines), commissioned 1966, the world's first large tidal-range power station, still in full operation

source.note: La Rance retrospective (ResearchGate record, 24 x 10 MW bulb turbines, still operating); read 2026-10-28
